Summary: The sources indicate that the "Attention is all you need" paper by Vaswani et al. was first published as a preprint in June 2017, but citation databases could not reliably detect its new frontier until later. In 2025, studies like "Attention Is All You Need In Speech Separation" and "DuSA: Fast and Accurate Dual-Stage Sparse Attention Mechanism" continued to build on the foundational work, exploring its applications in speech separation and dual-stage sparse attention mechanisms. However, there is also a study titled "Pure Attention Loses Rank Doubly Exponentially with Depth" that questions the scalability of pure attention with depth. Additionally, "Tabular Data: Is Attention All You Need?" compares attention-based architectures with gradient-boosted decision trees on tabular data. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on whether attention is all you need in all contexts.
